div.l: And set a soper at c̉ertayn prys
And we wiln rewled be at his deuys
In hyegh and lowh ⁊and þus bi oon assent
We ben accorded to þe Iuggement
And þer vppon þe wyn was fet a noon
We dronken and to reste went echoon
Wit outen eny leng taryinge
A morowe whan þe day gan to sprynge
Vp roos oure ost and was oure alde cok
And gaderede vs to gidere in a flok
And forþ we ryden a litel more þan pas
Vn to þe wateryng of seynt Thomas
And þere our oost gan his hors a reste
And seyde lordys herkenyth yf yow leste
Ye woot youre forward ⁊and I it yow recorde
If euynsong ⁊and morwesong accorde
Lat se Now ho shal telle þe firste tale
As eủere mote I. drinke wyn or ale
Who so be rebell to my Iuggement
Shall paye for all þat bi þe weye is spent
Now drawith Cut or þat we ferþ̉er twynne
Whoche þat hath þe shorteste shal be gynne
Sir knyght qd he my mayst̉er ⁊and my lord
Now drawyþ Cut for þat is myn accord
Comyþ Nere qd he my lady Prioresse
And ye sire Clerk lat be ȝour shamfastnesse
Ne studieth . nought lay hond to euery man
Anoon to drawe eủery wight be gan
And shortly for to tellen as it was
Were it bi auenture or sort or cas
The sothe is this þe cut fel te þᵉ knyght
Of which ful bliþe ⁊and glad was eủery whigt
And tellen he moste his tale as it was reson

And ye han herde what nedeþ wordes moo
And þan this goode man saugh þat it was soo
As he þat wys was and obedient
To kepen his forward bi his free assent
He seyde siþþen I shal by gynne þe game
